“For my part, when I enter most intimately into what I call…” — David Hume (Q0250)

An English quotation associated with Treatise I.4.6, organized here under self.

Quotes / David Hume / Q0250

English

For my part, when I enter most intimately into what I call myself, I always stumble on some particular perception or other.
Thinker David Hume
School Scottish Enlightenment
Source Treatise I.4.6
Theme Self

Source context

Archive record: this English passage is associated with Treatise I.4.6, within the Scottish Enlightenment tradition. Use the cited work or edition when a scholarly attribution is needed.

A short reading

Read in the register of self, the sentence asks the reader to test an assumption rather than to collect a slogan. In David Hume's wider work, similar claims are usually offered as prompts for judgment: what would have to be true for the sentence to hold, and what would follow if it did?
